concepts.name: Historical Evolution of Cotton Textile Industry in India
key_dimensions: First cotton textile mill established in Bombay (1854) vs. first jute mill in Rishra (1855) — chronological traps
Role of Cowasji Nanabhai Davar in establishing the industry and early entrepreneurship
Shift from hand-spinning (pre-industrial) to mill-based production and its socio-economic implications
Colonial-era tariff policies and their discriminatory impact on Indian cotton textiles vs. Manchester cloth

concepts.name: Three-Tier Structure: Mills, Powerlooms, and Handlooms
key_dimensions: Distinction between organized mill sector, decentralized powerloom sector, and handloom sector in terms of output share and employment
Handloom sector as the largest employer after agriculture — frequently tested fact
Powerloom sector contributing the highest share of fabric production (~60%) — common confusion with mill sector
Policy differences: Handloom Reservation Act provisions vs. open competition for powerlooms

concepts.name: Geographical Concentration and Locational Factors of Cotton Textile Mills
key_dimensions: Traditional concentration in Maharashtra (Mumbai) and Gujarat (Ahmedabad) — reasons: raw cotton proximity, humid climate, port access, capital availability
Shift of industry to southern states (Coimbatore, Chennai) and its reasons: cheap labor, hydroelectric power, local market
Mumbai as 'Cottonopolis of India' vs. Ahmedabad as 'Manchester of India' — frequently confused labels
Recent emergence of non-traditional centers (Ludhiana, Kanpur, Indore) and diversification trends

concepts.name: Raw Material Linkage: Cotton Production Regions and Mill Locations
key_dimensions: Black soil (Regur) belt and its role in cotton cultivation — states: Maharashtra, Gujarat, Madhya Pradesh, Telangana
Mismatch between raw cotton production zones and mill concentration zones — industry not always near raw material
Long-staple vs. short-staple cotton — India's dominance in short-staple and import dependency for long-staple for fine textiles
Impact of Bt cotton adoption on raw material availability and quality — linkage to Agricultural Biotechnology

concepts.name: Decline of Mumbai Mill Sector and Structural Shift
key_dimensions: Closure of composite mills in Mumbai post-1980s — reasons: high land cost, labor disputes, competition from powerlooms
1982 textile mill strike (led by Datta Samant) as a watershed event in Mumbai mill decline
Conversion of mill lands in Mumbai — legal battles, DCR (Development Control Regulations), and urban land use conflict
Shift of production to decentralized powerloom clusters in Surat, Bhiwandi, Ichalkaranji

concepts.name: Textile Policy Framework and Regulatory Bodies
key_dimensions: Textile Policy 1985 and National Textile Policy 2000 — key objectives and differences
Ministry of Textiles vs. Ministry of Commerce — jurisdictional overlap in export promotion
Textile Commissioner's office: functions, powers under Textiles (Development and Regulation) Order
Technology Upgradation Fund Scheme (TUFS) — purpose, sectors covered, and its revision to ATUFS (Amended TUFS)

concepts.name: Export Performance and Global Competitiveness of Indian Cotton Textiles
key_dimensions: India as the world's second-largest exporter of textiles and apparel — competition with China, Bangladesh, Vietnam
Post-MFA (Multi-Fibre Arrangement) expiry in 2005 — impact on Indian textile exports (both opportunity and threat)
Key export destinations: USA, EU, UAE — and the significance of FTAs in textile trade
Competitiveness gaps: low labor productivity, power costs, logistics vs. Bangladesh's duty-free access to EU

concepts.name: Integrated Textile Parks and Cluster Development Schemes
key_dimensions: Scheme for Integrated Textile Parks (SITP) — objectives, PPP model, and common infrastructure creation
Mega Integrated Textile Region and Apparel (MITRA) Parks — distinction from SITP, seven parks announced, strategic locations
Textile clusters vs. SEZs — difference in fiscal incentives and governance structure
PM MITRA vs. earlier schemes (TUFS, SITP) — UPSC trap on overlapping objectives

concepts.name: Handloom Sector: Significance, Challenges, and Government Support
key_dimensions: Handloom sector statistics: ~35 lakh handlooms, ~43 lakh weavers — largest cottage industry after agriculture
Geographical GI-tagged handloom products: Kanjivaram silk, Pochampally ikat, Chanderi, Banarasi — state-wise mapping
National Handloom Development Programme (NHDP) vs. Handloom Weavers' Comprehensive Welfare Scheme
Handloom Mark and India Handloom Brand — purpose, eligibility, and differences as quality certification mechanisms

concepts.name: Sericulture and Silk Sub-sector within Textile Industry
key_dimensions: India as the second-largest silk producer — four types of silk: Mulberry, Tasar, Eri, Muga (Muga exclusive to Assam — GI tagged)
Karnataka as the leading mulberry silk producer vs. Assam's monopoly on Muga silk — regional concentration trap
Central Silk Board (CSB) — statutory body under Ministry of Textiles; functions vs. Khadi and Village Industries Commission (KVIC)
Silk import competition from China — anti-dumping duties and their WTO implications

concepts.name: Technical Textiles: Emerging Segment and Policy Push
key_dimensions: Definition and classification of technical textiles: Agrotech, Meditech, Geotech, Protech, Sportech, etc. (12 segments)
National Technical Textiles Mission (NTTM) 2020–2025 — four components: Research, Promotion, Export, Education
India's low share in global technical textile market vs. potential — import substitution focus
Distinction between technical textiles and conventional textiles for policy and classification purposes

concepts.name: Man-Made Fibers (MMF) and Synthetic Textiles Segment
key_dimensions: India's underperformance in MMF segment vs. global trend where MMF dominates textile trade (~70% globally)
Historical inverted duty structure on MMF — raw material taxed higher than finished goods; recent corrections
Surat as the hub of synthetic/MMF textile production — polyester fabric dominance
Strategic importance of MMF for export competitiveness — National Fiber Policy recommendations

concepts.name: Production Linked Incentive (PLI) Scheme for Textiles
key_dimensions: PLI for textiles focused on MMF apparel, MMF fabrics, and technical textiles — deliberate exclusion of cotton apparel (trap question)
Eligibility criteria: minimum investment thresholds and incremental turnover conditions
Objectives: scale, technology, global supply chain integration — distinction from MITRA parks
States competing for PLI investments and their textile ecosystems

concepts.name: Environmental Concerns and Sustainability in Cotton Textile Industry
key_dimensions: Water-intensive nature of cotton cultivation and textile processing — virtual water trade concept
Textile dyeing and effluent discharge — Tirupur cluster and its Noyyal river pollution controversy
Zero Liquid Discharge (ZLD) norms — applicability to textile units, NGT orders, compliance challenges
Sustainable cotton initiatives: Better Cotton Initiative (BCI), organic cotton certification and India's participation

concepts.name: Khadi and Village Industries: Institutional and Philosophical Dimensions
key_dimensions: Khadi and Village Industries Commission (KVIC) — statutory body under KVIC Act 1956, under Ministry of MSME (not Ministry of Textiles — common trap)
Distinction between Khadi (hand-spun AND hand-woven) vs. handloom (machine-spun but hand-woven) — definitional trap
Mahatma Gandhi's philosophy of Swadeshi and Khadi as economic decentralization vs. industrial textile production
PMEGP (Prime Minister's Employment Generation Programme) — implemented through KVIC, linkage to cottage textile units

concepts.name: Labor Dynamics and Employment in Cotton Textile Industry
key_dimensions: Cotton textile industry as one of the largest employers in manufacturing sector — ~45 million direct and indirect jobs
Feminization of labor in garment and apparel segment vs. male-dominated mill sector
Industrial Relations: applicability of Industrial Disputes Act to textile mills vs. cottage sector exemptions
Skill gap issues and Samarth scheme (Scheme for Capacity Building in Textile Sector) for worker training

concepts.name: Coimbatore and South Indian Textile Hub: Comparative Geography
key_dimensions: Coimbatore as 'Manchester of South India' — reasons: proximity to cotton in northern Tamil Nadu, hydropower from Western Ghats, entrepreneurial community
Tirupur as global knitwear hub — export contribution, supply chain ecosystem, buyer-driven commodity chain
Ichalkaranji and Bhiwandi (Maharashtra) as powerloom clusters — distinction from mill-based production
Comparison of northern (Kanpur, Ludhiana) vs. southern textile centers on raw material, power, and export orientation

concepts.name: India's Cotton Cultivation: Linkage between Agriculture and Industry
key_dimensions: India as the largest cotton producer and largest consumer of cotton — balance between domestic use and export of raw cotton
Cotton Corporation of India (CCI) — price support mechanism, MSP procurement, and buffer stock role
Impact of raw cotton export policy (restrictions/bans) on domestic textile industry competitiveness
Relationship between cotton price volatility and powerloom/mill sector profitability — economic geography linkage

concepts.name: Apparel and Garment Export Ecosystem: Value Chain Analysis
key_dimensions: Difference between textile exports (fabric/yarn) and apparel exports (finished garments) — India's weakness in moving up the value chain
Apparel Export Promotion Council (AEPC) vs. Cotton Textiles Export Promotion Council (TEXPROCIL) — roles and sector coverage
China+1 strategy and India's positioning to capture garment orders — constraints: labor laws, logistics, lead time
Bangladesh's competitive advantage (lower wages, duty-free EU access under EBA) vs. India's strengths in cotton availability

concepts.name: Institutional Framework: Promotional Bodies and Councils in Textile Sector
key_dimensions: Mapping of export promotion councils: TEXPROCIL (cotton), AEPC (apparel), SRTEPC (synthetic), HEPC (handlooms), SEPC (silk) — sector-specific traps
Textile Research Associations (TRAs) — ATIRA, BTRA, SITRA, NITRA — regional distribution and research mandates
National Institute of Fashion Technology (NIFT) — statutory body under Ministry of Textiles; design and skill development
Overlap and coordination challenges between Ministry of Textiles, Ministry of MSME, and Ministry of Commerce in textile governance
